source: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (MoHFW) & National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) India Air Quality Health Advisories; CPCB NAQI
disclaimer: Informational guidance only — not medical advice. Consult a qualified doctor or healthcare professional for symptoms, diagnosis, or treatment.

categories.label: Good
categories.generalAdvice: Air quality is satisfactory with minimal impact. Normal outdoor activity and natural cross-ventilation are generally appropriate.

familyAdvice.children: Normal outdoor play is fine; continue routine hydration and clean indoor cooking habits.
familyAdvice.older_adults: Normal walks and light outdoor activity are suitable.
familyAdvice.breathing_heart: Routine daily activities are generally comfortable; keep prescribed rescue medication accessible as usual.
familyAdvice.pregnancy: Normal outdoor light activity and fresh-air ventilation are suitable.

categories.label: Satisfactory
categories.generalAdvice: Acceptable air quality, though unusually sensitive people may experience minor breathing discomfort on prolonged exertion.

familyAdvice.children: Outdoor play is okay, but prefer lower-traffic hours and avoid playing next to busy roads.
familyAdvice.older_adults: Keep brisk walks to early morning or cleaner hours; rest if tired.
familyAdvice.breathing_heart: Consider shortening intense outdoor exertion and keep indoor cooking exhaust running.
familyAdvice.pregnancy: Prefer parks or low-traffic streets during cleaner hours; avoid passive smoke and incense indoors.

categories.label: Moderate
categories.generalAdvice: May cause breathing discomfort to people with lung or heart conditions, children, and older adults. Time outdoor activities to the cleanest hours.

familyAdvice.children: Limit vigorous outdoor sports during peak traffic hours; use indoor play during afternoon/evening spikes.
familyAdvice.older_adults: Shift walks indoors or to the cleanest low-PM window; monitor for breathlessness or fatigue.
familyAdvice.breathing_heart: Reduce outdoor exertion, wear a well-fitted N95/KN95 mask outdoors if needed, and run HEPA filtration in the sleeping room.
familyAdvice.pregnancy: Minimize time near traffic corridors; ventilate only during the cleanest 2-3 hour window and run indoor filtration.

categories.label: Poor
categories.generalAdvice: May cause breathing discomfort to most people on prolonged exposure. Keep windows closed during peak hours and shift strenuous activity indoors.

familyAdvice.children: Keep children indoors during smog peaks; avoid outdoor school/park sports and maintain a filtered clean room.
familyAdvice.older_adults: Stay indoors as much as possible; avoid early-morning cold smog if PM2.5 is high and keep living spaces sealed.
familyAdvice.breathing_heart: Stay indoors with a clean-room HEPA purifier running; avoid all outdoor exertion and contact your physician promptly if symptoms worsen.
familyAdvice.pregnancy: Avoid outdoor exposure during poor-AQI hours; use a properly sized HEPA purifier in the bedroom and avoid incense/smoke.

categories.label: Very Poor
categories.generalAdvice: May cause respiratory illness on prolonged exposure. Avoid outdoor physical exertion, seal leaky windows, and prioritize a clean room indoors.

familyAdvice.children: Keep indoors continuously during episode; set up the bedroom as a clean room and avoid dry sweeping.
familyAdvice.older_adults: Remain indoors in a filtered room; avoid sudden cold air drafts and wear a fitted N95 if stepping out is unavoidable.
familyAdvice.breathing_heart: High risk of symptom flare-ups; stay in a filtered clean room, keep emergency care plan handy, and consult your doctor proactively.
familyAdvice.pregnancy: Stay indoors in a clean room with continuous HEPA filtration and zero indoor combustion or fragrance sprays.

categories.label: Severe
categories.generalAdvice: Health emergency conditions: everyone may be affected. Stay indoors, keep windows closed, run air filtration continuously, and use fitted N95 masks if travel is unavoidable.

familyAdvice.children: Strictly keep indoors in a sealed clean room; postpone non-essential outdoor travel and monitor closely for cough or wheezing.
familyAdvice.older_adults: Remain in the cleanest indoor room with continuous HEPA filtration; seek medical attention immediately for chest discomfort or shortness of breath.
familyAdvice.breathing_heart: Emergency-level precaution: stay in a continuous HEPA clean room, avoid all outdoor air, and follow your physician's action plan.
familyAdvice.pregnancy: Remain indoors in a filtered clean room, eliminate all indoor smoke/frying fumes, and wear an N95 mask if essential travel is required.

familyProfiles.label: Children & infants
familyProfiles.rationale: Higher breathing rate per kg body weight and developing lungs increase sensitivity to fine particulate matter.

familyProfiles.label: Older adults (65+)
familyProfiles.rationale: Age-related cardiovascular and respiratory changes increase sensitivity during high-PM2.5 episodes.

familyProfiles.label: Breathing or heart conditions
familyProfiles.rationale: Conditions like asthma, COPD, bronchitis, or cardiovascular disease are aggravated by PM2.5 spikes.

familyProfiles.label: Pregnancy
familyProfiles.rationale: Reducing sustained PM2.5 exposure helps protect maternal respiratory comfort and household air quality.
